name: memfd_secret
description: memfd_secret() creates an anonymous RAM-based file and returns a file descriptor that refers to it, providing stronger protection for memory regions. The file is automatically released when all references are closed, and its size can be set using ftruncate(2).

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags to control the behavior, such as FD_CLOEXEC to set the close-on-exec flag.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: The per-process limit on the number of open file descriptors has been reached.
The system-wide limit on the total number of open files has been reached.
There was insufficient memory to create a new anonymous file.
memfd_secret() is not implemented on this architecture, or has not been enabled on the kernel command-line with secretmem_enable=1.

bugs: No 100% guarantee that the kernel won’t access memory ranges backed by memfd_secret() in all circumstances; may impact system performance and is disabled by default, requiring kernel parameter enablement.
